act: Bradford Lee Folk & The Bluegrass Playboys
intro: A Colorado bluegrass singer with a high, lonesome sound.
story: Bradford Lee Folk was born in Louisiana and raised in Missouri, and in Colorado he fronted Open Road, a bluegrass band that made three albums for Rounder. He once told Westword that the old style of bluegrass is not palatable to the general public, and he played it anyway. He brought the Bluegrass Playboys to Pickathon in 2013. The next spring he released Somewhere Far Away, after moving to Tennessee and farming by day. In 2025 and 2026 he reunited with Open Road for a run of new singles, among them Rainy Season in September 2026.

intro: A Portland country band, back after 2007.
story: Caleb Klauder had come to Pickathon in 2001 and 2007, and in 2013 he brought his country band, with Rusty Blake on pedal steel and Reeb Willms on vocals. Willms had joined Foghorn Stringband on guitar and vocals in the winter of 2011, and Klauder plays with Foghorn and in Cajun Country Revival too. He later formed a duo with Willms, and the two played Pickathon in 2016 and 2018.

intro: A supergroup of Spoon and Wolf Parade.
story: Divine Fits began in 2011, when Britt Daniel of Spoon emailed a demo to Dan Boeckner of Wolf Parade and Handsome Furs, and Boeckner added vocals in his kitchen. The song was "What Gets You Alone." A Thing Called Divine Fits came out on Merge in August 2012, with the drummer Sam Brown, their only album, and they played Pickathon the next summer. After the tour, both went back to other projects, and the band has played only a one-off reunion at a Boeckner show in Brooklyn.

intro: A Portland old-time band, here for the seventh time.
story: The founders of Foghorn Stringband met at the National Oldtime Fiddlers' Contest in Weiser, Idaho, in 2000. In the winter of 2011, Reeb Willms joined on guitar and vocals, making the lineup Klauder, Lind, Landry and Willms, and the Portland Mercury ranked them among the finest practitioners of old-time music on the globe in September 2012. They played Pickathon again in 2013, a seventh visit, and once more in 2016. They still tour internationally.

intro: A towering voice in traditional Appalachian singing.
story: Ginny Hawker, born in 1940, sings the ballads of Appalachia. In 1988 she met Tracy Schwarz of the New Lost City Ramblers at a fiddle camp, and the two became husband and harmony partners. Their Good Songs for Hard Times came out in 2000 and Draw Closer, on Rounder, in 2004. They came to Pickathon in 2013. Tracy Schwarz died on March 29, 2025, at 86.

Howe Gelb was born in Wilkes-Barre, Pennsylvania, in 1956 and moved to Tucson in the late 1970s. He started Giant Sandworms, which became Giant Sand, and has led it ever since. He released the solo Snarl Some Piano in 2011 and Giant Sand's Tucson: A Country Rock Opera in 2012, and came to Pickathon in 2013, two years before the band did. In 2018 he went back to the Giant Sand name with Returns to Valley of Rain, re-recording the 1985 debut. Fire Records pressed his 2001 album Confluence on vinyl for the first time.

intro: A Dublin band of Irish storytelling and string-band drive.
story: I Draw Slow is a Dublin five-piece built around the siblings Dave and Louise Holden, blending Irish folk with American bluegrass and old-time. Redhills, their second album, came out in 2011, and they played Pickathon in 2013, then again in 2016. White Wave Chapel followed in early 2014, and The Irish Times called it a kind of greengrass and something special. They still tour internationally.

intro: A Portland bluegrass band, here for the sixth time.
story: Jackstraw are a Portland bluegrass quartet, known since 1994 for a gritty, honky-tonk-inflected sound. Their guitarist said in a 2012 interview that they had played nearly every Pickathon since the festival began, and by 2013 they were back for the sixth time, after 2001, 2003, 2005, 2007 and 2009. They came again in 2022, and have stayed loyal to home, recently playing a Portland FolkMusic Society show.

intro: A Texas honky-tonk songwriter of plainspoken storytelling.
story: Leo Rondeau was raised in the Turtle Mountains of North Dakota and moved to Austin, where he played the White Horse most Thursdays. Down at the End of the Bar, in 2009, earned him a Songwriter of the Year nomination from the Academy of Texas Music, and Take It and Break It came out in March 2013, months before his Pickathon set. He later moved to Nashville and recorded Right On Time, which Saving Country Music reviewed, calling him an Austin honky-tonk fixture. In November 2026 he played the White Horse again, with Sentimental Family Band and Kristina Murray.

intro: Moody synth-rock from the Black Mountain family.
story: Lightning Dust began in 2007 as a side project for two members of Black Mountain, Amber Webber and Joshua Wells, in Vancouver. After two quieter albums, Fantasy came out on Jagjaguwar on June 25, 2013, a shift to synths and drum machine, and Exclaim! called it their most consistent and cohesive effort. They had played Pickathon in 2011 and returned that summer. In 2017 Webber and Wells left Black Mountain to focus on Lightning Dust, and Spectre came in 2019 and Nostalgia Killer in 2023.
artist_reel_line: They left Black Mountain in 2017 to make Spectre and Nostalgia Killer.

intro: A North Carolina troubadour of gravelly folk-blues.
story: Malcolm Holcombe was born in Weaverville, North Carolina, on September 2, 1955, and played in local bands as a teenager. His folk-blues had been on record since 1994 when he played Pickathon in 2013. Pretty Little Troubles, his 15th album, came out in 2017, produced by Darrell Scott, and No Depression called him an Appalachian ghost story and Americana enigma. He died on March 9, 2024, in Asheville, at age 68.

intro: A keyboardist of groove-heavy piano experiments.
story: Marco Benevento made his name in the Benevento/Russo Duo with the drummer Joe Russo, and in 2006 toured with Trey Anastasio's band. As a piano trio he made Invisible Baby, on Hyena in 2007, and Me Not Me in 2009, which All About Jazz called the inaugural stone delight of 2009. He played Pickathon in 2013 and returned in 2014. He later joined Joe Russo's Almost Dead and recorded his ninth solo album, Benevento, alone at his Woodstock studio. Glera came out on Big Crown in 2026.

intro: A Portland band of gritty harmonies.
story: Old Light are a Portland band of gritty Americana and multipart harmonies. Their 2010 debut was The Dirty Future, and in 2011 they recorded a Pumphouse Session at Pickathon, the year of their first set. They returned in 2013, the year they released a five-tape series, starting with NO in March, after a KEXP session and Northwest dates.

intro: British Columbia banjo makers and harmony singers.
story: Pharis and Jason Romero are a husband-and-wife duo from Horsefly, British Columbia, where Jason builds banjos as J. Romero Banjos. Their record A Passing Glimpse won New/Emerging Artist of the Year at the 2012 Canadian Folk Music Awards, and they came to Pickathon in 2013. A Wanderer I'll Stay won the Juno for Traditional Roots Album of the Year in 2016, and Sweet Old Religion won it again. These Are the Days That Turn into Years came out in 2026.

Sallie Ford left college in 2006 and moved from North Carolina to Portland, where she waited tables and met her bandmates while busking. Willamette Week named them Portland's best new band in 2010. Dirty Radio came out on Partisan in May 2011, the year they played Letterman, and they opened for the Avett Brothers and Mavis Staples and toured with Thao & Mirah. Untamed Beast came in February 2013, and they played Pickathon that summer, their second visit after 2010. The Summer EP came in December, and on December 17, 2013, they announced a split after four final shows. Ford has made solo albums since, including Soul Sick on Vanguard in 2017.

intro: A Portland band of percussive banjo folk-rock.
story: The members of the Builders and the Butchers moved independently from Alaska to Portland and began busking, and within a year Northwest press called them among the region's best new groups. Ryan Sollee had come down from Alaska in 2003 and earlier led the hardcore band the Born Losers. Salvation Is a Deep Dark Well came out on Gigantic on June 16, 2009, produced by Chris Funk with more than 50 guest musicians, and NPR called "Devil Town" music to dance, sweat, weep and rejoice to. They played Pickathon in 2011 and 2013. Scattered across the country, they reconvened for No Tomorrow on Badman Recording Co.

intro: A Texas king of juke-joint swing.
story: Wayne Hancock was born on May 1, 1965, joined the Marines in 1983 and wrote "Cold Lonesome Wind" on deployment in Okinawa. He moved to Austin in 1990. His debut, Thunderstorms and Neon Signs, produced by Lloyd Maines, came out on Dejadisc in 1995 and was reissued on Ark 21 in 1998; the nickname The Train came from three-to-five-hour shows. Hank Williams III covered two of his songs on Risin' Outlaw in 1999. He played Pickathon in 2008 and 2013, and cut Slingin' Rhythm with Maines in 2016.
artist_reel_line: Hank III covered two of his songs; he cut Slingin' Rhythm in 2016.

story: Sam Cohen is a Brooklyn guitarist and songwriter who came from the Boston psychedelic group Apollo Sunshine. Yellowbirds released Songs from the Vanished Frontier on Royal Potato Family on May 28, 2013, after the debut The Color. Spectrum Culture called their Pickathon set that summer the punchiest of the weekend. The band wrapped up in 2014, and Cohen came back to the farm in 2015.
